URL: https://www.ipsos.com/en-uk/reform-uk-holds-slim-voting-intention-lead-over-labour-andy-burnham-preferred-pm-nigel-farage-and
(WebFetch — Ipsos, fieldwork 25-30 June 2026, 1,045 GB adults 18+)

Voting intention: Reform UK 26%, Labour 24%, Conservatives 18%, Green 13%, Liberal Democrats 11%.
Preferred Prime Minister: Andy Burnham 30%, Nigel Farage 16%, Kemi Badenoch 13%.
Keiran Pedley (Director of Politics, Ipsos): "With Labour narrowing the gap with Reform UK, public doubts over whether Reform UK or the Conservatives are ready for government and Andy Burnham preferred as Prime Minister to Kemi Badenoch and Nigel Farage, Labour will be more optimistic about the future than they were a month ago."

Cross-reference — Survation (approved):
URL: https://www.survation.com/labour-draw-level-with-reform-in-starmers-last-days-how-much-improvement-can-burnham-make/
(Search snippet — Survation's own reporting) Survation's final Westminster voting-intention poll with Keir Starmer as leader (fieldwork 10-14 July 2026) had Labour and Reform UK tied on 24% each — Labour up five points on the 17 June poll, their largest single upward movement since the 2024 General Election; Reform down three, their lowest share since weeks after the May 2025 local elections.
